title: Brake Check & Pad/Rotor Service
subtitle: Brakes are a safety system — we'll inspect first, then decide DIY pad/rotor work vs a shop. You've got this.
tone: Safety-first coach. Encourage inspection DIY; be honest when pad/rotor replacement exceeds comfort. Never rush bleeding or torque.
prerequisites: Level ground, parking brake understanding for your drivetrain (EPB procedures differ)
Torque specs for lug nuts (door sticker / manual)
tools_checklist: Lug wrench or torque wrench + socket
Optional: pad spreader, torque sticks, EPB scan tool
parts_checklist: Rotors if below min thickness or heavily scored (often replace in pairs on an axle)
Brake hardware kit / shims if not included
Brake fluid DOT rating matching the cap (only if bleeding)

adaptive_rules.coach_note: Many pads first come due in the 30–70k window depending on traffic and hills. Inspect before they squeal into metal-on-metal.
Trucks that tow or haul eat pads/rotors faster. Check rears too — trucks often wear unevenly axle-to-axle.
If you have an electronic parking brake, rear calipers often need a scan tool to retract. Don't force the piston — that's a shop moment unless you have the right tool.
Wear sensors and electronic warnings are common. Clearing faults and bedding pads correctly matters — indie brake specialist is a strong option.
Soft pedal, pulling, ABS light, or fluid loss = stop DIY diagnosis and get professional help before driving further.

steps.title: Brake health check-in
steps.description: Tell me what you're feeling — squeal, grind, vibration, longer stopping distance — or if this is a mileage inspection. We'll start with a visual check before any parts come off.
steps.safety_warning: If the pedal sinks, ABS/brake lights are on, or fluid is leaking, do not drive — arrange a tow / shop visit.

action_buttons.label: I have symptoms — diagnose
action_buttons.payload: Brake symptoms: describe noise, pedal feel, and when it happens. My mileage is in the garage profile.

steps.title: Lift one corner safely
steps.description: Loosen lugs on the ground slightly, jack at the correct point, stand the car, then remove the wheel. Keep lugs in a magnetic tray so nothing rolls under the car.
steps.safety_warning: Jack stands only — never work beside a tire with the car on a jack alone. Support the vehicle before you put your hands near the rotor.

steps.title: Read the pad & rotor
steps.description: Check outer and inner pad thickness (inners often wear faster). Look for uneven wear, cracked pads, groove-deep rotor scoring, or blue heat spots. Compare to the chart.
steps.safety_warning: Metal-on-metal grinding means stop driving hard and replace ASAP — rotors are likely damaged.

variants.description: At higher mileage, also peek at brake hoses for cracks and the fluid color in the reservoir (don't open yet unless bleeding).

steps.title: DIY job or brake specialist?
steps.description: Front pads on a simple floating caliper are a solid DIY for many owners (~1.5–3 hours/axle). Electronic parking brakes, seized slides, or needed fluid bleeds push this toward a shop — that's smart, not failure.
steps.safety_warning: Brakes are safety-critical. If torque specs, EPB service mode, or bleeding make you unsure, book a pro.

variants.description: EPB / sensor note: rears may need a scan tool. If you don't have one, do fronts only DIY or let the shop do the axle that needs EPB retract.
variants.safety_warning: Forcing an EPB caliper open can destroy the motor. Use service mode or a shop.

steps.title: Replace pads (and rotors if needed)
steps.description: Hang the caliper from a hook/wire — don't let it dangle on the hose. Compress the piston slowly, install hardware, pads, and rotor if replacing. Caliper bolts torqued to spec.
steps.safety_warning: Never twist or stress the brake hose. If the reservoir overflows while compressing, remove a little fluid with a clean syringe — keep DOT fluid off paint.

action_buttons.label: Piston / slides stuck
action_buttons.payload: Brake caliper piston or slides are stuck during pad replacement. What are safe next steps?

steps.title: Wheel on — torque matters
steps.description: Refit the wheel, snug lugs on the stand, lower the car, then torque in a star pattern to the door-sticker spec. Pump the brake pedal until firm before you move the car.
steps.safety_warning: Driving with a soft pedal is unsafe. If the pedal stays soft after pumping, do not drive — reopen the chat or tow.

action_buttons.label: Pedal still soft
action_buttons.payload: After brake work my pedal is soft. Walk me through safe checks before I consider driving.

steps.title: Bed-in & log the service
steps.description: Do a gentle bed-in (a series of moderate stops from ~35–45 mph without coming to a full panic stop). Avoid hard stops and car washes for a short stretch. Log pads/rotors and mileage in your health file.
steps.safety_warning: Leave extra following distance for the first drive. Pull over if you smell heavy burning or the pedal changes feel.

action_buttons.label: Show bed-in details
action_buttons.payload: Give me a clear bed-in procedure for new brake pads on my vehicle.

completion.title: Brake service wrapped — drive gently at first
completion.description: You treated a safety system with respect. Re-torque lugs after 25–50 miles. Next inspection often aligns with tire rotations (~5–8k miles) unless a wear sensor returns sooner.

action_buttons.label: Still have a noise
action_buttons.payload: I still hear a brake noise after service. Help me narrow it down.
